findings.title: Arbitrary graph cycles can replace valid foundation outlines
findings.body: BuildLoops accepts the first cycle found from each starting line and immediately marks all of that cycle's lines as used, before ProcessPoints determines whether it represents a valid rectangle. In branching or shared-edge CAD linework, such as two adjacent rectangular foundations, DFS can select the combined outer perimeter or another cycle instead of the individual rectangles. The selected cycle consumes edges needed by the intended outlines, so the command can create one incorrectly sized foundation or omit valid foundations entirely. Loop candidates must be geometrically validated before consuming their edges, with deterministic handling for multiple cycles and shared edges.

findings.title: Loop search has exponential worst-case behavior
findings.body: FindLoopIterative enumerates simple paths by copying the complete line and index lists for every branch. The loop.Count guard does not impose an effective limit because repeated indices are already prohibited, so dense or junction-heavy CAD layers can generate exponentially many search states and large allocation pressure. Because this runs synchronously on Revit's UI thread before the transaction, a complex or malformed selected drawing can freeze the application. Add bounded traversal and cancellation/complexity limits, or use a graph cycle algorithm designed for planar linework.
